content.title: About
content.content: Wheat crackers are crisp baked snacks made from wheat flour, water, salt, and sometimes a small amount of vegetable oil. They are commonly enjoyed as a snack, accompaniment to soups, or as a base for sandwiches. The crackers have a light, dry texture and a neutral flavor that pairs well with a variety of toppings and dips.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Crackers originated in medieval Europe as a way to preserve bread.
Wheat crackers are often used in Italian cuisine for making breadcrumb coatings.
They can be plain or flavored with herbs, spices, and seeds.
In many countries crackers are served with hot dishes to add a crunchy element.
Low moisture content allows crackers to be stored for long periods.

items.title: Source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: Wheat crackers provide slowly digestible carbs that can help sustain fullness over time.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Traditional crackers contain virtually no fat, making them suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Rich in dietary fiber
items.content: When made from whole‑grain wheat flour, crackers can be a good source of fiber that supports digestive health.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Wheat flour supplies thiamine, niacin, and folate, which are important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Versatile base for nutrient‑dense meals
items.content: Crackers can be topped with protein (cheese, deli meat) and vegetables, enhancing the overall nutritional profile of a snack.

items.title: Wheat allergy or gluten intolerance
items.content: People with celiac disease or wheat allergy should avoid wheat crackers as they can trigger reactions.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Dry wheat crackers can raise blood sugar quickly, which is a consideration for individuals with diabetes.

items.title: Salt content
items.content: Some varieties contain added salt; those monitoring sodium intake should choose low‑salt options.

items.title: Possible additives
items.content: Crackers may contain preservatives, flavor enhancers, or artificial sweeteners that not everyone tolerates.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Crackers can be eaten straight from the package, used as a base for sandwiches, added to soups and salads for crunch, or crushed and used as a breadcrumb coating for meat and fish. They also pair well with cheeses, pâtés, hummus, and vegetable dips.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store crackers in an airtight container in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. Properly stored, they remain crisp for several months. Discard any crackers that develop a stale odor or off‑flavor.
